title: Fit a downlight trim overhead: squeeze each torsion spring shut and thread it up through its bracket slot, flange flush
instruction: Install the recessed-light trim in the ceiling housing above you: hook both of its torsion springs into the housing's brackets and push the trim up until its flange sits flat on the ceiling, then let go.
context: Electricians (O*NET 47-2111, about 760,000 US jobs; task: install lighting fixtures) finish every recessed downlight by fitting its trim into the housing in the ceiling. A torsion-spring trim has two V-shaped wire springs. Each spring's legs must be squeezed shut between finger and thumb and passed up through a narrow slot in a bracket inside the can; let go, they spread and hook above it. The brackets sit at whatever angle the housing was installed, so the trim must be turned until each spring is under its slot, which is seen only by looking up into the can. With one spring in, the trim hangs crooked from it while the other goes in; then the trim is pushed up until the flange sits flat on the ceiling, held there by the springs. Here each hand squeezes one spring. Legs only 3 degrees open no longer pass the slot, and a hand under the ceiling has little room: the drywall is just above the fingers.
setup: Station table in front of two YAM arms (bases 61 cm apart), overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions in cm: x forward from the line between the arm bases, y to the robot's left of their midpoint. (1) Ceiling mock-up: 1/2 in. (12.7 mm) gypsum board over one joist bay, 44 x 34 cm between two 2x6 joists, underside 120 cm above the floor (45 cm above the table top), on two 2x4 posts with a header at its far end. A work light (a lamp only, no stand modelled) shines up from 25 cm below. A 6-3/4 in. (171 mm) cut-out at x 30, y 0 holds a 6 in. IC airtight recessed housing (steel can, 172 mm inside diameter, 19 cm tall above the ceiling) with a BR30 LED lamp in its socket, face 6.5 cm above the ceiling. Inside the can, two torsion-spring brackets face each other across the can: steel tabs 1.5 mm thick, top 20 mm above the ceiling's underside, each with a 5 x 16 mm slot (long side tangential) on a 158 mm circle. The brackets' line is turned from the robot's left-right line by phi, drawn per trial from 3.5 to 5 deg either way. (2) Trim: 6 in. shallow baffle trim with torsion springs, white, 0.30 kg: flange 194 mm OD, baffle 148 mm at the flange tapering to 116 mm, 75 mm tall; two torsion springs on opposite sides (1.6 mm music wire, coil 6 mm above the flange, two 70 mm legs each with 3 mm outward tip hooks, legs spread about 50 deg each side when free). It rests flange-down on its carton (15 x 15 x 12 cm) on the table at x 30, y 0, springs pointing up, its spring line turned within 3 deg of the left-right line and at least 4 deg away from the brackets' angle; carton moved up to 1.5 cm in x and 0.6 cm in y (all from the trial seed). Named check setups (phi, trim) in deg: (-4.5, 2), (4, -2), (5, 1), (-3.5, 2.5), (3.5, -2.5).
scoring: Read at the end of the trial, with the robot not touching the trim (person check in brackets). 1.0 (ends the trial): both springs captured, i.e. both legs of each spring pass up through its bracket's slot with the tips above the tab (look up into the can past the flange; the trim stays up when let go), and the flange flat on the ceiling: gap between flange and ceiling at most 2 mm all round (a 2 mm feeler does not enter anywhere; sim: 12 points at radius 92 mm), trim still for 1 s. 0.5: both springs captured, flange not flush. 0.25: one spring captured (trim hangs from it). 0: no spring captured (trim on the carton, dropped, resting on its springs under the brackets, or still held).
reset_notes: Squeeze each spring and pull the trim down out of the housing, put it back flange-down on its carton with its springs at the next setup's angle (marks on the carton every 1 deg), and turn the housing's brackets to the next setup's angle (marks on the drywall round the cut-out). Setups run in order 0-4.
fidelity: Isaac Lab-Arena yam_arena, PhysX (CPU) 480 Hz, 20 Hz control, full-size parts. Ceiling at 1.20 m (reach), drywall over one joist bay. Trim and four spring legs are free bodies; each leg on a hinge, its spring a torque computed from the leg angle (0.11 N m/rad, free 50 deg) with a stiff stop where the legs meet. Capture, pull-up and seating are contact only, no snaps. Dimensions representative. Full statement: README.
run_limit: 2000 control steps (100 s at 20 Hz). The trial also ends as soon as the score reaches 1.0.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (seed 0, 2,000 steps). Scripted demo: 1.0 in the official Inspect Robots run (default seed, 944 of 2,000 steps); 1.0 twice, identical, at the default seed; 1.0 at seed 7. Doing nothing: 0. Demo replayed open-loop at seed 3: 0. Trim not turned: 0.
